original_question: Is NPH estimated to have a higher prevalence rate among persons aged 65 or older compared to congenital hydrocephalus?

final_qi.question: What is the prevalence rate of NPH among persons aged 65 or older?
final_qi.long_answer: Epidemiologic surveys in community-dwelling older adults show that idiopathic normal-pressure hydrocephalus is present in roughly one out of every 200 people aged 65 years or older, giving a prevalence of about 0.5 percent in this age group.

final_qi.question: What is the prevalence rate of congenital hydrocephalus among persons aged 65 or older?
final_qi.long_answer: Population-based estimates from the U.S. National Health Interview Survey indicate that congenital hydrocephalus is reported in roughly 4 persons per 10 000 among adults aged ≥ 65 years, equivalent to about 0.04 % of that age group. This low prevalence reflects the rarity of the defect at birth and the limited proportion of affected individuals who survive into older adulthood.
